intended_object: The canonical morphism of schemes Proj S → Proj S^{(n)} (n > 0) induced by the inclusion of the n-th Veronese subring S^{(n)} = ⊕_j S_{nj} into an ℕ-graded commutative ring S. On points it sends p to p ∩ S^{(n)}, and it is the forward arrow of the Veronese isomorphism. Inferred from the module docstring, the name, and its use in `schemeIso`.
explanation: `VeroneseRing 𝒮 n = ⨁ j, 𝒮 (n*j)` with `component` grading and `inclusion` the canonical ring map is the standard Veronese subring. `degreeScaledMap` glues the chart maps Spec(S_{(ι f)}) → Spec(S^{(n)}_{(f)}). These come from the localization maps S^{(n)}_{(f)} → S_{(ι f)}, for homogeneous f of positive degree. The glued map is defined on the union of the D₊(ι f). `domain_eq_top` shows this union is all of Proj S: if s has positive degree and lies outside p, then sⁿ lies in S^{(n)} and also lies outside p. Composing with that identification gives exactly the classical morphism. The supporting lemmas confirm this: `forward_pointIdeal` shows points go to their contraction, and `forward_restrict_chart` shows the restriction to each chart is Spec of the canonical localization map. The setting is an arbitrary ℕ-graded commutative ring with any n > 0, which is the natural generality; n > 0 is necessary. Mathlib has no Veronese construction. The docstring is oddly worded but consistent with the definition.
